source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Social/Political Life Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Family — The First Community
points: The **family** is the smallest and first **community** a person belongs to.

sub: **Nuclear family** — parents and their children only.
**Blended family** — formed when families join (e.g. through remarriage).

points: Families provide **care, values, security and identity** and are changing over time (more nuclear families in cities).

sections.heading: 2. From Family to Community
points: A **community** is a group of people connected by something shared — **place, language, work, religion or interests**.
We each belong to **many communities at once** (family, neighbourhood, school, region, nation).
Communities widen from **local** (village/town) to **regional** and finally to the **national community** — all Indians.

sections.heading: 3. Living Together — Values
points: Living in communities needs values: **cooperation, sharing, tolerance, respect for diversity** and helping one another.
**Interdependence** — members depend on each other (e.g. farmers, teachers, doctors, cleaners).
Differences of religion, language and custom are respected — the spirit of **unity in diversity**.
**Duties and responsibilities** come with belonging to a community.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Family = first/smallest community; types = nuclear, joint, blended.
Community = people sharing place, language, work, religion or interests.
We belong to many communities at once; widening circles → the national community.
Living together needs cooperation, tolerance, respect and interdependence.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **nuclear** family = parents + children; a **joint** family = several generations together — don't swap.
A person belongs to **many** communities simultaneously, not just one.
Community bonds can be based on many things (place, work, language) — not only religion.
